# robots.txt - iowaprintsolutions.com
#
# ===========================================================================
# CRITICAL: DO NOT DISALLOW /assets/, *.js, OR *.css
# ===========================================================================
# This site is a client-side React single-page app. dist/index.html ships an
# empty <div id="root"> - every page's content, headings, links, and meta tags
# are produced by the JavaScript bundle in /assets/.
#
# A previous version of this file contained:
#     Disallow: /assets/
#     Disallow: /*.js$
#     Disallow: /*.css$
#
# That forbade crawlers from fetching the only files that render the site, so
# any crawler respecting robots.txt saw a blank page on every URL. Blocking
# render-critical resources on a client-rendered site is self-inflicted
# deindexing. Google's own guidance is explicit that JS and CSS needed for
# rendering must remain crawlable.
#
# If bundle size or crawl budget ever becomes a concern, the answer is
# pre-rendering or SSR - never blocking the bundle.
# ===========================================================================

User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://iowaprintsolutions.com/sitemap.xml

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traditional search engines
#
# No Crawl-delay directives. Google ignores Crawl-delay entirely, and Bing
# honours it - so the only thing the old "Crawl-delay: 1" achieved was slowing
# Bing down for no benefit. Crawl rate is better managed in Search Console or
# Bing Webmaster Tools if it is ever actually a problem.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
User-agent: Googlebot
Allow: /

User-agent: Googlebot-Image
Allow: /

User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /

User-agent: DuckDuckBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Applebot
Allow: /

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AI search and answer engines
#
# These are allowed deliberately. Being the cited source when someone asks an
# assistant about print management software in Iowa is a primary goal for this
# site, and a crawler that cannot read a page cannot cite it.
#
# Note that training crawlers and search crawlers are SEPARATE user agents per
# vendor. To stay citable in AI answers while opting out of model training,
# block the training agent and keep the search agent allowed - do not block a
# whole vendor. The split below keeps that choice available.
#
# "Claude-Web" was removed: it is a retired user agent, replaced by ClaudeBot
# for crawling and Claude-SearchBot / Claude-User for retrieval.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Retrieval / answer-time crawlers (keep allowed to remain citable) ---
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /

User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Claude-User
Allow: /

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /

User-agent: Perplexity-User
Allow: /

User-agent: DuckAssistBot
Allow: /

User-agent: MistralAI-User
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-CloudVertexBot
Allow: /

# --- Training / dataset crawlers ---
# Allowed: presence in model weights helps brand and product recall in
# assistant answers even when no live citation occurs. Switch any of these to
# "Disallow: /" to opt out of training without losing AI-search citations.
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /

User-agent: anthropic-ai
Allow: /

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /

User-agent: Meta-ExternalAgent
Allow: /

User-agent: Amazonbot
Allow: /

User-agent: cohere-ai
Allow: /

User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths with no search value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal diagnostic pages
Disallow: /analytics-test
Disallow: /debug-assets.html
Disallow: /debug-20250826.html
Disallow: /test-deploy.txt

# Search results are thin and parameterised - not useful in an index
Disallow: /search
